blocks.text: Light and other forms of electromagnetic radiation travel as waves made of oscillating electric and magnetic fields. The waves are described by their wavelength (lambda) and frequency (nu), and they travel at the speed of light, c = 3.0 x 10^8 m/s. These are related by c = lambda x nu, where lambda is in metres, nu in hertz (s^-1) and c in m/s.
The electromagnetic spectrum includes radio waves, microwaves, infrared radiation, visible light, ultraviolet radiation, X-rays and gamma rays.

blocks.alt: A horizontal band divided into gamma ray, X-ray, ultra violet, a narrow visible strip, infrared, microwave and radio frequency, from highest energy on the left to lowest energy on the right. Above it a wavelength scale from 10^-2 to 10^12 nm increasing to the right; below it a frequency scale from 10^20 to 10^4 s^-1 increasing to the left. The visible strip is opened out below into a colour band from 400 nm (violet) to 750 nm (red), labelled visible region.
blocks.caption: Figure 29.1: Electromagnetic spectrum showing wavelength, frequency, energy, and the visible light region (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 29.1).

blocks.text: According to Planck's quantum theory, atoms and molecules emit or absorb only discrete amounts of energy (quanta), and the energy of radiation is directly proportional to its frequency: E = h nu, where h is Planck's constant, 6.626 x 10^-34 J s.
